segments.text: Hello and welcome all of you to UE. My name is Philip and today I'm going to
give you a brief induction of the most useful facility for every student, the
library. This is the place where you are expected to spend most of your time to
advance your knowledge for a successful academic life. First, regarding opening
hours, our library here in French A campus gives students 24-hour access
during academic terms. For those of you who would like to use the libraries in
Bauer Ashton and Glenside campuses, they are only open from 7.30 a.m. till
midnight. The Alexandra warehouse library in Glouchester campus is
currently unavailable as it's being renovated to a more modern facility to
meet the university's new standards. However, you can still go to other
campuses libraries as long as you bring a valid student card. Despite the
long opening hours there will be no library staff working on Sundays. On weekdays you can always find
help from librarians from 8 30 a.m to 6 30 p.m. The times are shorter on Saturdays running only
six hours from 10 a.m. Now to some changes we've made recently. Since many of you have reported a
lack of textbooks during exam time starting from this term we decided to reduce the length of time
one can borrow a textbook by half.
This means you can now only borrow those for 30 days
instead of 60, like other materials,
and they are non-renewable.
The maximum number of items you can bring home
at any one time remains unchanged at 20.
Also, from this term, we've introduced two new services,
click and collect, and scan and deliver.
The former helps you to reduce the time
you spend browsing at the library as it can be crowded at times and the latter
sends you electronic copies of your requested materials to your email. To use
these services, find and fill the request form on our website. You'll be informed
by email when your items are available to collect and they will be held for up
to 10 days. If you're unable to pick up your items within the specified
period then please contact the campus you intend to pick the item up from. Do
Do check the opening hours before you visit.
For scan and deliver, due to the matter of copyright, we can only scan up to one chapter
of a book, one journal article, or up to 5% of an item and email it to you.
Requests will be refused where we have existing electronic access to an item.
